prompt: Prepare a noisy two-person interview for podcast delivery from 48 kHz/24-bit WAV stems. One speaker is 9 dB quieter, HVAC noise is audible in pauses, and aggressive denoising produces metallic consonants. Define and apply an edit/mix chain that preserves speech intelligibility, controls dynamics without pumping, reaches the specified integrated loudness/true-peak target, keeps mono compatibility, and verifies the final encoded file rather than only the DAW preview. Video editing is out of scope.

loudness, true-peak, mono, and encoded-file inspection evidence

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual audio-production boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=human-experience; near-neighbor=video-production), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Define listening context, source quality, sample rate/bit depth, edit intent, noise floor, dynamics, EQ, stereo/spatial image, loudness target, true peak, music/dialog balance, and delivery codec.
The delivered encode meets the declared loudness/peak envelope while speech artifacts and intelligibility are judged from the processed final file, not inferred from meters alone.

Monitor on representative speakers/headphones at multiple levels, inspect clipping/noise/artifacts, measure loudness/true peak where relevant, check mono compatibility, edits, fades, silence, metadata, and final encoded file.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not normalize blindly to peak level, over-denoise until speech artifacts appear, compress every source heavily, or judge a mix from one playback system alone.
